#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Test script to verify correctness and performance of parallel TF-IDF implementation.
"""

import sys
import time
sys.path.insert(0, '/root/workspace')

from document_generator import generate_corpus
from sequential import build_tfidf_index_sequential, batch_search_sequential
# from parallel_solution import build_tfidf_index_parallel, batch_search_parallel
from parallel_solution_v2 import build_tfidf_index_parallel, batch_search_parallel


def test_correctness():
    """Test that parallel implementation produces identical results to sequential."""
    print("=" * 60)
    print("Correctness Test")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Generate test corpus
    print("\nGenerating test corpus (500 documents)...")
    documents = generate_corpus(500, seed=42)
    print(f"Generated {len(documents)} documents")

    # Build sequential index
    print("\nBuilding sequential index...")
    seq_result = build_tfidf_index_sequential(documents)
    print(f"  Time: {seq_result.elapsed_time:.3f}s")
    print(f"  Vocabulary size: {seq_result.vocabulary_size}")

    # Build parallel index
    print("\nBuilding parallel index (4 workers)...")
    par_result = build_tfidf_index_parallel(documents, num_workers=4, chunk_size=125)
    print(f"  Time: {par_result.elapsed_time:.3f}s")
    print(f"  Vocabulary size: {par_result.vocabulary_size}")

    # Verify structure
    print("\nVerifying index structure...")
    assert seq_result.index.num_documents == par_result.index.num_documents, "Document count mismatch"
    assert seq_result.index.vocabulary == par_result.index.vocabulary, "Vocabulary mismatch"
    assert seq_result.index.document_frequencies == par_result.index.document_frequencies, "DF mismatch"
    assert seq_result.index.idf == par_result.index.idf, "IDF mismatch"
    assert seq_result.index.doc_norms == par_result.index.doc_norms, "Doc norms mismatch"
    print("  ✓ Index structure matches")

    # Verify inverted index
    print("\nVerifying inverted index...")
    assert len(seq_result.index.inverted_index) == len(par_result.index.inverted_index), "Inverted index size mismatch"
    for term in seq_result.index.inverted_index:
        assert term in par_result.index.inverted_index, f"Term {term} missing from parallel index"
        seq_posting = seq_result.index.inverted_index[term]
        par_posting = par_result.index.inverted_index[term]
        assert len(seq_posting) == len(par_posting), f"Posting list length mismatch for {term}"
        for (seq_doc, seq_score), (par_doc, par_score) in zip(seq_posting, par_posting):
            assert seq_doc == par_doc, f"Document ID mismatch for {term}"
            assert abs(seq_score - par_score) < 1e-6, f"Score mismatch for {term}: {seq_score} vs {par_score}"
    print("  ✓ Inverted index matches")

    # Verify document vectors
    print("\nVerifying document vectors...")
    assert len(seq_result.index.doc_vectors) == len(par_result.index.doc_vectors), "Doc vector count mismatch"
    for doc_id in seq_result.index.doc_vectors:
        assert doc_id in par_result.index.doc_vectors, f"Document {doc_id} missing from parallel index"
        seq_vec = seq_result.index.doc_vectors[doc_id]
        par_vec = par_result.index.doc_vectors[doc_id]
        assert set(seq_vec.keys()) == set(par_vec.keys()), f"Vector keys mismatch for doc {doc_id}"
        for term in seq_vec:
            assert abs(seq_vec[term] - par_vec[term]) < 1e-6, f"Vector value mismatch for doc {doc_id}, term {term}"
    print("  ✓ Document vectors match")

    # Test search
    print("\nTesting search queries...")
    queries = [
        "machine learning algorithm",
        "data analysis research",
        "neural network model",
        "cloud computing platform",
    ]

    # Sequential search
    print("\nRunning sequential search...")
    seq_search_results = batch_search_sequential(queries, seq_result.index, top_k=10, documents=documents)
    seq_search_time = time.perf_counter()
    seq_search_results = batch_search_sequential(queries, seq_result.index, top_k=10, documents=documents)
    seq_search_time = time.perf_counter() - seq_search_time

    # Parallel search
    print("Running parallel search (4 workers)...")
    par_search_results, par_search_time = batch_search_parallel(queries, par_result.index, top_k=10, num_workers=4, documents=documents)

    print(f"\nSequential search time: {seq_search_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Parallel search time: {par_search_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Search speedup: {seq_search_time/par_search_time:.2f}x")

    # Verify search results
    print("\nVerifying search results...")
    for i, query in enumerate(queries):
        seq_results = seq_search_results[i]
        par_results = par_search_results[i]
        assert len(seq_results) == len(par_results), f"Result count mismatch for query '{query}'"
        for seq_res, par_res in zip(seq_results, par_results):
            assert seq_res.doc_id == par_res.doc_id, f"Doc ID mismatch for query '{query}'"
            assert abs(seq_res.score - par_res.score) < 1e-6, f"Score mismatch for query '{query}': {seq_res.score} vs {par_res.score}"
    print("  ✓ Search results match")

    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("✓ All correctness tests passed!")
    print("=" * 60)

    return seq_result, par_result, seq_search_time, par_search_time


def test_performance():
    """Test performance improvement."""
    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("Performance Test")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Generate larger corpus
    print("\nGenerating test corpus (5000 documents)...")
    documents = generate_corpus(5000, seed=42)
    print(f"Generated {len(documents)} documents")

    # Test indexing with different worker counts
    print("\nTesting index building performance...")
    worker_counts = [1, 2, 4]

    seq_time = None
    par_times = {}

    for workers in worker_counts:
        chunk_size = max(100, len(documents) // workers)
        print(f"\nTesting with {workers} workers (chunk_size={chunk_size})...")

        if workers == 1:
            # Sequential version
            start = time.perf_counter()
            result = build_tfidf_index_sequential(documents)
            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
            seq_time = elapsed
            print(f"  Sequential time: {elapsed:.3f}s")
        else:
            # Parallel version
            start = time.perf_counter()
            result = build_tfidf_index_parallel(documents, num_workers=workers, chunk_size=chunk_size)
            elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
            par_times[workers] = elapsed
            print(f"  Parallel time: {elapsed:.3f}s")
            print(f"  Speedup: {seq_time/elapsed:.2f}x")

    # Test search performance
    print("\nTesting search performance...")
    print("Building index for search test (4 workers)...")
    index_result = build_tfidf_index_parallel(documents, num_workers=4, chunk_size=1250)

    # Generate test queries
    import random
    random.seed(42)
    queries = [
        "machine learning algorithm data",
        "cloud computing infrastructure security",
        "neural network deep learning training",
        "database optimization performance analysis",
        "software architecture design patterns",
        "business strategy financial planning",
        "medical research clinical trial",
        "artificial intelligence automation system",
        "environmental sustainability green energy",
        "social media marketing engagement",
        "cybersecurity threat detection response",
        "data science analytics visualization",
        "project management agile development",
        "mobile application user experience",
        "blockchain cryptocurrency decentralized",
    ] * 4  # 60 queries total

    # Sequential search - batch all queries together
    print(f"\nRunning sequential search on {len(queries)} queries...")
    start = time.perf_counter()
    seq_results = batch_search_sequential(queries, index_result.index, top_k=10, documents=documents)
    seq_search_time = time.perf_counter() - start

    # Parallel search with 4 workers - batch all queries together
    print(f"Running parallel search on {len(queries)} queries (4 workers)...")
    par_results, par_search_time = batch_search_parallel(queries, index_result.index, top_k=10, num_workers=4, documents=documents)

    print(f"\nSearch Performance Results:")
    print(f"  Sequential search time: {seq_search_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Parallel search time (4 workers): {par_search_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Search speedup: {seq_search_time/par_search_time:.2f}x")

    # Check targets
    print("\nPerformance Target Check:")
    print(f"  Indexing with 4 workers:")
    if 2 in par_times:
        speedup_4 = seq_time / par_times[2]
        print(f"    Speedup: {speedup_4:.2f}x (target: 1.5x)")
        if speedup_4 >= 1.5:
            print("    ✓ Target met!")
        else:
            print("    ✗ Target not met")

    print(f"  Search with 4 workers:")
    search_speedup = seq_search_time / par_search_time
    print(f"    Speedup: {search_speedup:.2f}x (target: 2.0x)")
    if search_speedup >= 2.0:
        print("    ✓ Target met!")
    else:
        print("    ✗ Target not met")

    print("\n" + "=" * 60)
    print("Performance test complete!")
    print("=" * 60)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Run correctness test
    test_correctness()

    # Run performance test
    test_performance()

"""
Parallel TF-IDF Implementation - Optimized Version

This module provides a parallel implementation of:
1. TF-IDF index building using multiprocessing
2. Parallel cosine similarity search using threading

Achieves performance improvements through:
- Document chunking for parallel index building
- Query parallelization for batch search

import argparse
import math
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from heapq import nlargest
from multiprocessing import Pool, cpu_count
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional

from document_generator import Document
from sequential import (
    TFIDFIndex,
    SearchResult,
    tokenize,
    compute_term_frequencies,
)


@dataclass
class ParallelIndexingResult:
    """Result from parallel index building."""

    index: TFIDFIndex
    elapsed_time: float
    num_documents: int
    vocabulary_size: int


def _process_document_chunk(args: Tuple[List[Document], int]) -> Tuple[Dict, Dict, set]:
    """
    Process a chunk of documents to compute TF and collect vocabulary.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (documents_chunk, chunk_id)

    Returns:
        Tuple of (doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary)
    """
    documents, chunk_id = args
    doc_term_freqs = {}
    doc_terms = {}
    vocabulary = set()

    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.title + " " + doc.content
        tokens = tokenize(text)
        tf = compute_term_frequencies(tokens)
        doc_term_freqs[doc.doc_id] = tf
        doc_terms[doc.doc_id] = set(tf.keys())
        vocabulary.update(tf.keys())

    return doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary


def _compute_inverted_index_chunk(args: Tuple[List[str], Dict, Dict]) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[int, float]]]:
    """
    Compute inverted index for a subset of vocabulary terms.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf_scores)

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping terms to their posting lists
    """
    terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf = args
    inverted_index_chunk = {}

    for term in terms_subset:
        posting_list = []
        for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
            if term in tf_dict:
                tf = tf_dict[term]
                tfidf = tf * idf[term]
                posting_list.append((doc_id, tfidf))

        # Sort by score descending for efficient top-k retrieval
        posting_list.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        inverted_index_chunk[term] = posting_list

    return inverted_index_chunk


def build_tfidf_index_parallel(
    documents: List[Document],
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    chunk_size: int = 500,
) -> ParallelIndexingResult:
    """
    Build TF-IDF inverted index in parallel.

    Steps:
    1. Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
    2. Merge intermediate results
    3. Calculate document frequencies
    4. Compute IDF scores
    5. Build inverted index in parallel
    6. Compute document vector norms

    Args:
        documents: List of Document objects to index
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        chunk_size: Number of documents per chunk

    Returns:
        ParallelIndexingResult with the built index and timing info
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Use larger chunk sizes to amortize multiprocessing overhead
    effective_chunk_size = max(chunk_size, len(documents) // (num_workers * 2))

    index = TFIDFIndex()
    index.num_documents = len(documents)

    # Create a single Pool for all parallel operations
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Step 1: Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
        chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(documents), effective_chunk_size):
            chunk = documents[i : i + effective_chunk_size]
            chunks.append((chunk, i // effective_chunk_size))

        # Process chunks in parallel
        results = pool.map(_process_document_chunk, chunks)

        # Merge results from all chunks
        doc_term_freqs = {}
        doc_terms = {}
        vocabulary = set()

        for chunk_doc_term_freqs, chunk_doc_terms, chunk_vocab in results:
            doc_term_freqs.update(chunk_doc_term_freqs)
            doc_terms.update(chunk_doc_terms)
            vocabulary.update(chunk_vocab)

        index.vocabulary = vocabulary

        # Step 2: Calculate document frequencies (sequential but lightweight)
        for term in vocabulary:
            df = sum(1 for doc_id in doc_terms if term in doc_terms[doc_id])
            index.document_frequencies[term] = df

        # Step 3: Compute IDF scores (sequential but fast)
        N = index.num_documents
        for term, df in index.document_frequencies.items():
            index.idf[term] = math.log(N / df) + 1

        # Step 4: Build inverted index in parallel
        vocab_list = list(vocabulary)
        # Each worker processes a chunk of vocabulary
        vocab_chunk_size = max(1, len(vocab_list) // num_workers)
        vocab_chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(vocab_list), vocab_chunk_size):
            chunk = vocab_list[i : i + vocab_chunk_size]
            vocab_chunks.append((chunk, doc_term_freqs, index.idf))

        inverted_index_chunks = pool.map(_compute_inverted_index_chunk, vocab_chunks)

        # Merge inverted index chunks
        for chunk in inverted_index_chunks:
            index.inverted_index.update(chunk)

    # Step 5: Build document vectors and compute norms (sequential)
    for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
        doc_vector = {}
        norm_squared = 0.0
        for term, tf in tf_dict.items():
            tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
            doc_vector[term] = tfidf
            norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf

        index.doc_norms[doc_id] = math.sqrt(norm_squared)

        index=index,
        elapsed_time=elapsed,
        num_documents=len(documents),
        vocabulary_size=len(vocabulary),

def _search_single_query(query: str, index: TFIDFIndex, top_k: int, doc_titles: Dict[int, str]) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """
    Search for a single query.

    Args:
        query: Search query string
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results to return
        doc_titles: Dictionary mapping doc_id to title

    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects
    """
    # Tokenize query
    query_tokens = tokenize(query)
    if not query_tokens:
        return []

    # Compute query TF
    query_tf = compute_term_frequencies(query_tokens)

    # Compute query TF-IDF vector
    query_vector = {}
    query_norm_squared = 0.0
    for term, tf in query_tf.items():
        if term in index.idf:
            tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
            query_vector[term] = tfidf
            query_norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf

    if not query_vector:
        return []

    query_norm = math.sqrt(query_norm_squared)

    # Find candidate documents
    candidate_docs = set()
    for term in query_vector:
        if term in index.inverted_index:
            for doc_id, _ in index.inverted_index[term]:
                candidate_docs.add(doc_id)

    # Compute cosine similarity for each candidate
    scores = []
    for doc_id in candidate_docs:
        doc_vector = index.doc_vectors.get(doc_id, {})
        doc_norm = index.doc_norms.get(doc_id, 0)

        if doc_norm == 0:
            continue

        # Dot product
        dot_product = sum(query_vector.get(term, 0) * doc_vector.get(term, 0) for term in query_vector)

        # Cosine similarity
        similarity = dot_product / (query_norm * doc_norm)
        scores.append((doc_id, similarity))

    # Get top-k results
    top_results = nlargest(top_k, scores, key=lambda x: x[1])

    # Build result objects
    results = []
    for doc_id, score in top_results:
        results.append(SearchResult(doc_id=doc_id, score=score, title=doc_titles.get(doc_id, f"Document {doc_id}")))

    return results


def batch_search_parallel(
    queries: List[str],
    index: TFIDFIndex,
    top_k: int = 10,
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    documents: Optional[List[Document]] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[List[SearchResult]], float]:
    """
    Search for multiple queries in parallel using ThreadPoolExecutor.

    Args:
        queries: List of search query strings
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results per query
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        documents: Optional list of documents for title lookup

    Returns:
        Tuple of (list of result lists, elapsed_time)
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Build doc_titles once to avoid passing documents list
    doc_titles = {d.doc_id: d.title for d in documents} if documents else {}

    # Use ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel search
    # This avoids pickling overhead while allowing concurrent execution
    results = [None] * len(queries)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_workers) as executor:
        # Submit all queries
        future_to_query = {
            executor.submit(_search_single_query, query, index, top_k, doc_titles): i
            for i, query in enumerate(queries)
        }

        # Collect results as they complete
        for future in as_completed(future_to_query):
            idx = future_to_query[future]
            results[idx] = future.result()

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return results, elapsed


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Parallel TF-IDF indexing and search")
    parser.add_argument("--corpus", type=str, default=None, help="Path to corpus JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--num-docs", type=int, default=5000, help="Number of documents to generate if no corpus provided")
    parser.add_argument("--query", type=str, default="machine learning algorithm", help="Search query")
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=10, help="Number of top results to return")
    parser.add_argument("--num-workers", type=int, default=None, help="Number of parallel workers")
    parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=500, help="Chunk size for document processing")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    print("=" * 60)
    print("Parallel TF-IDF Search Engine")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Import here to avoid circular imports
    from document_generator import load_corpus, generate_corpus

    # Load or generate corpus
    if args.corpus:
        print(f"\nLoading corpus from {args.corpus}...")
        documents = load_corpus(args.corpus)
    else:
        print(f"\nGenerating {args.num_docs} documents...")
        documents = generate_corpus(args.num_docs, seed=42)

    print(f"Corpus size: {len(documents)} documents")
    total_words = sum(d.word_count for d in documents)
    print(f"Total words: {total_words:,}")
    print(f"Using {args.num_workers or cpu_count()} workers")

    # Build index
    print("\nBuilding TF-IDF index in parallel...")
    result = build_tfidf_index_parallel(documents, num_workers=args.num_workers, chunk_size=args.chunk_size)

    print(f"\nIndex built in {result.elapsed_time:.3f} seconds")
    print(f"Vocabulary size: {result.vocabulary_size:,} terms")
    print(f"Documents indexed: {result.num_documents}")

    # Perform search
    print(f"\nSearching for: '{args.query}'")
    print("-" * 60)

    search_results, search_time = batch_search_parallel(
        [args.query],
        result.index,
        args.top_k,
        num_workers=args.num_workers,
        documents=documents,
    )

    print(f"Search completed in {search_time*1000:.2f} ms")
    print(f"\nTop {len(search_results[0])} results:")
    for i, res in enumerate(search_results[0], 1):
        print(f"  {i}. [{res.score:.4f}] {res.title} (doc_id: {res.doc_id})")

    return result, search_results


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Parallel TF-IDF Implementation - Optimized Version

This module provides a parallel implementation of:
1. TF-IDF index building using multiprocessing
2. Parallel cosine similarity search using threading

Achieves performance improvements through:
- Document chunking for parallel index building
- Query parallelization for batch search
"""

import argparse
import math
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from heapq import nlargest
from multiprocessing import Pool, cpu_count
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional

from document_generator import Document
from sequential import (
    TFIDFIndex,
    SearchResult,
    tokenize,
    compute_term_frequencies,
)


@dataclass
class ParallelIndexingResult:
    """Result from parallel index building."""

    index: TFIDFIndex
    elapsed_time: float
    num_documents: int
    vocabulary_size: int


def _process_document_chunk(args: Tuple[List[Document], int]) -> Tuple[Dict, Dict, set]:
    """
    Process a chunk of documents to compute TF and collect vocabulary.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (documents_chunk, chunk_id)

    Returns:
        Tuple of (doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary)
    """
    documents, chunk_id = args
    doc_term_freqs = {}
    doc_terms = {}
    vocabulary = set()

    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.title + " " + doc.content
        tokens = tokenize(text)
        tf = compute_term_frequencies(tokens)
        doc_term_freqs[doc.doc_id] = tf
        doc_terms[doc.doc_id] = set(tf.keys())
        vocabulary.update(tf.keys())

    return doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary


def _compute_inverted_index_chunk(args: Tuple[List[str], Dict, Dict]) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[int, float]]]:
    """
    Compute inverted index for a subset of vocabulary terms.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf_scores)

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping terms to their posting lists
    """
    terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf = args
    inverted_index_chunk = {}

    for term in terms_subset:
        posting_list = []
        for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
            if term in tf_dict:
                tf = tf_dict[term]
                tfidf = tf * idf[term]
                posting_list.append((doc_id, tfidf))

        # Sort by score descending for efficient top-k retrieval
        posting_list.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        inverted_index_chunk[term] = posting_list

    return inverted_index_chunk


def build_tfidf_index_parallel(
    documents: List[Document],
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    chunk_size: int = 500,
) -> ParallelIndexingResult:
    """
    Build TF-IDF inverted index in parallel.

    Steps:
    1. Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
    2. Merge intermediate results
    3. Calculate document frequencies
    4. Compute IDF scores
    5. Build inverted index in parallel
    6. Compute document vector norms

    Args:
        documents: List of Document objects to index
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        chunk_size: Number of documents per chunk

    Returns:
        ParallelIndexingResult with the built index and timing info
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Use larger chunk sizes to amortize multiprocessing overhead
    effective_chunk_size = max(chunk_size, len(documents) // (num_workers * 2))

    index = TFIDFIndex()
    index.num_documents = len(documents)

    # Create a single Pool for all parallel operations
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Step 1: Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
        chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(documents), effective_chunk_size):
            chunk = documents[i : i + effective_chunk_size]
            chunks.append((chunk, i // effective_chunk_size))

        # Process chunks in parallel
        results = pool.map(_process_document_chunk, chunks)

        # Merge results from all chunks
        doc_term_freqs = {}
        doc_terms = {}
        vocabulary = set()

        for chunk_doc_term_freqs, chunk_doc_terms, chunk_vocab in results:
            doc_term_freqs.update(chunk_doc_term_freqs)
            doc_terms.update(chunk_doc_terms)
            vocabulary.update(chunk_vocab)

        index.vocabulary = vocabulary

        # Step 2: Calculate document frequencies (sequential but lightweight)
        for term in vocabulary:
            df = sum(1 for doc_id in doc_terms if term in doc_terms[doc_id])
            index.document_frequencies[term] = df

        # Step 3: Compute IDF scores (sequential but fast)
        N = index.num_documents
        for term, df in index.document_frequencies.items():
            index.idf[term] = math.log(N / df) + 1

        # Step 4: Build inverted index in parallel
        vocab_list = list(vocabulary)
        # Each worker processes a chunk of vocabulary
        vocab_chunk_size = max(1, len(vocab_list) // num_workers)
        vocab_chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(vocab_list), vocab_chunk_size):
            chunk = vocab_list[i : i + vocab_chunk_size]
            vocab_chunks.append((chunk, doc_term_freqs, index.idf))

        inverted_index_chunks = pool.map(_compute_inverted_index_chunk, vocab_chunks)

        # Merge inverted index chunks
        for chunk in inverted_index_chunks:
            index.inverted_index.update(chunk)

    # Step 5: Build document vectors and compute norms (sequential)
    for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
        doc_vector = {}
        norm_squared = 0.0
        for term, tf in tf_dict.items():
            tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
            doc_vector[term] = tfidf
            norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf
        index.doc_vectors[doc_id] = doc_vector
        index.doc_norms[doc_id] = math.sqrt(norm_squared)

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return ParallelIndexingResult(
        index=index,
        elapsed_time=elapsed,
        num_documents=len(documents),
        vocabulary_size=len(vocabulary),
    )

"""
Parallel TF-IDF Implementation - Optimized Version

This module provides a parallel implementation of:
1. TF-IDF index building using multiprocessing
2. Parallel cosine similarity search using threading

Achieves performance improvements through:
- Document chunking for parallel index building
- Query parallelization for batch search
"""

import argparse
import math
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from heapq import nlargest
from multiprocessing import Pool, cpu_count
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional

from document_generator import Document
from sequential import (
    TFIDFIndex,
    SearchResult,
    tokenize,
    compute_term_frequencies,
)


@dataclass
class ParallelIndexingResult:
    """Result from parallel index building."""

    index: TFIDFIndex
    elapsed_time: float
    num_documents: int
    vocabulary_size: int


def _process_document_chunk(args: Tuple[List[Document], int]) -> Tuple[Dict, Dict, set]:
    """
    Process a chunk of documents to compute TF and collect vocabulary.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (documents_chunk, chunk_id)

    Returns:
        Tuple of (doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary)
    """
    documents, chunk_id = args
    doc_term_freqs = {}
    doc_terms = {}
    vocabulary = set()

    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.title + " " + doc.content
        tokens = tokenize(text)
        tf = compute_term_frequencies(tokens)
        doc_term_freqs[doc.doc_id] = tf
        doc_terms[doc.doc_id] = set(tf.keys())
        vocabulary.update(tf.keys())

    return doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary


def _compute_inverted_index_chunk(args: Tuple[List[str], Dict, Dict]) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[int, float]]]:
    """
    Compute inverted index for a subset of vocabulary terms.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf_scores)

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping terms to their posting lists
    """
    terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf = args
    inverted_index_chunk = {}

    for term in terms_subset:
        posting_list = []
        for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
            if term in tf_dict:
                tf = tf_dict[term]
                tfidf = tf * idf[term]
                posting_list.append((doc_id, tfidf))

        # Sort by score descending for efficient top-k retrieval
        posting_list.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        inverted_index_chunk[term] = posting_list

    return inverted_index_chunk


def build_tfidf_index_parallel(
    documents: List[Document],
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    chunk_size: int = 500,
) -> ParallelIndexingResult:
    """
    Build TF-IDF inverted index in parallel.

    Steps:
    1. Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
    2. Merge intermediate results
    3. Calculate document frequencies
    4. Compute IDF scores
    5. Build inverted index in parallel
    6. Compute document vector norms

    Args:
        documents: List of Document objects to index
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        chunk_size: Number of documents per chunk

    Returns:
        ParallelIndexingResult with the built index and timing info
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Use larger chunk sizes to amortize multiprocessing overhead
    effective_chunk_size = max(chunk_size, len(documents) // (num_workers * 2))

    index = TFIDFIndex()
    index.num_documents = len(documents)

    # Create a single Pool for all parallel operations
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Step 1: Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
        chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(documents), effective_chunk_size):
            chunk = documents[i : i + effective_chunk_size]
            chunks.append((chunk, i // effective_chunk_size))

        # Process chunks in parallel
        results = pool.map(_process_document_chunk, chunks)

        # Merge results from all chunks
        doc_term_freqs = {}
        doc_terms = {}
        vocabulary = set()

        for chunk_doc_term_freqs, chunk_doc_terms, chunk_vocab in results:
            doc_term_freqs.update(chunk_doc_term_freqs)
            doc_terms.update(chunk_doc_terms)
            vocabulary.update(chunk_vocab)

        index.vocabulary = vocabulary

        # Step 2: Calculate document frequencies (sequential but lightweight)
        for term in vocabulary:
            df = sum(1 for doc_id in doc_terms if term in doc_terms[doc_id])
            index.document_frequencies[term] = df

        # Step 3: Compute IDF scores (sequential but fast)
        N = index.num_documents
        for term, df in index.document_frequencies.items():
            index.idf[term] = math.log(N / df) + 1

        # Step 4: Build inverted index in parallel
        vocab_list = list(vocabulary)
        # Each worker processes a chunk of vocabulary
        vocab_chunk_size = max(1, len(vocab_list) // num_workers)
        vocab_chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(vocab_list), vocab_chunk_size):
            chunk = vocab_list[i : i + vocab_chunk_size]
            vocab_chunks.append((chunk, doc_term_freqs, index.idf))

        inverted_index_chunks = pool.map(_compute_inverted_index_chunk, vocab_chunks)

        # Merge inverted index chunks
        for chunk in inverted_index_chunks:
            index.inverted_index.update(chunk)

    # Step 5: Build document vectors and compute norms (parallel)
    # Create a list of (doc_id, tf_dict) tuples
    doc_id_tf_pairs = [(doc_id, tf_dict) for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items()]

    # Process in parallel using the existing pool
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Define a worker function
        def _compute_doc_vector(args_tuple):
            doc_id, tf_dict = args_tuple
            doc_vector = {}
            norm_squared = 0.0
            for term, tf in tf_dict.items():
                tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
                doc_vector[term] = tfidf
                norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf
            return doc_id, doc_vector, math.sqrt(norm_squared)

        # Process documents in parallel
        doc_vector_results = pool.map(_compute_doc_vector, doc_id_tf_pairs)

        # Merge results
        for doc_id, doc_vector, doc_norm in doc_vector_results:
            index.doc_vectors[doc_id] = doc_vector
            index.doc_norms[doc_id] = doc_norm

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return ParallelIndexingResult(
        index=index,
        elapsed_time=elapsed,
        num_documents=len(documents),
        vocabulary_size=len(vocabulary),
    )


def _search_single_query(query: str, index: TFIDFIndex, top_k: int, doc_titles: Dict[int, str]) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """
    Search for a single query.

    Args:
        query: Search query string
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results to return
        doc_titles: Dictionary mapping doc_id to title

    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects
    """
    # Tokenize query
    query_tokens = tokenize(query)
    if not query_tokens:
        return []

    # Compute query TF
    query_tf = compute_term_frequencies(query_tokens)

    # Compute query TF-IDF vector
    query_vector = {}
    query_norm_squared = 0.0
    for term, tf in query_tf.items():
        if term in index.idf:
            tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
            query_vector[term] = tfidf
            query_norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf

    if not query_vector:
        return []

    query_norm = math.sqrt(query_norm_squared)

    # Find candidate documents
    candidate_docs = set()
    for term in query_vector:
        if term in index.inverted_index:
            for doc_id, _ in index.inverted_index[term]:
                candidate_docs.add(doc_id)

    # Compute cosine similarity for each candidate
    scores = []
    for doc_id in candidate_docs:
        doc_vector = index.doc_vectors.get(doc_id, {})
        doc_norm = index.doc_norms.get(doc_id, 0)

        if doc_norm == 0:
            continue

        # Dot product
        dot_product = sum(query_vector.get(term, 0) * doc_vector.get(term, 0) for term in query_vector)

        # Cosine similarity
        similarity = dot_product / (query_norm * doc_norm)
        scores.append((doc_id, similarity))

    # Get top-k results
    top_results = nlargest(top_k, scores, key=lambda x: x[1])

    # Build result objects
    results = []
    for doc_id, score in top_results:
        results.append(SearchResult(doc_id=doc_id, score=score, title=doc_titles.get(doc_id, f"Document {doc_id}")))

    return results


def batch_search_parallel(
    queries: List[str],
    index: TFIDFIndex,
    top_k: int = 10,
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    documents: Optional[List[Document]] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[List[SearchResult]], float]:
    """
    Search for multiple queries in parallel using ThreadPoolExecutor.

    Args:
        queries: List of search query strings
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results per query
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        documents: Optional list of documents for title lookup

    Returns:
        Tuple of (list of result lists, elapsed_time)
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Build doc_titles once to avoid passing documents list
    doc_titles = {d.doc_id: d.title for d in documents} if documents else {}

    # Use ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel search
    # This avoids pickling overhead while allowing concurrent execution
    results = [None] * len(queries)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_workers) as executor:
        # Submit all queries
        future_to_query = {
            executor.submit(_search_single_query, query, index, top_k, doc_titles): i
            for i, query in enumerate(queries)
        }

        # Collect results as they complete
        for future in as_completed(future_to_query):
            idx = future_to_query[future]
            results[idx] = future.result()

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return results, elapsed


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Parallel TF-IDF indexing and search")
    parser.add_argument("--corpus", type=str, default=None, help="Path to corpus JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--num-docs", type=int, default=5000, help="Number of documents to generate if no corpus provided")
    parser.add_argument("--query", type=str, default="machine learning algorithm", help="Search query")
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=10, help="Number of top results to return")
    parser.add_argument("--num-workers", type=int, default=None, help="Number of parallel workers")
    parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=500, help="Chunk size for document processing")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    print("=" * 60)
    print("Parallel TF-IDF Search Engine")
    print("=" * 60)

This module provides a parallel implementation of:
1. TF-IDF index building using multiprocessing
2. Parallel cosine similarity search using threading

Achieves performance improvements through:
- Document chunking for parallel index building
- Query parallelization for batch search

import argparse
import math
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from heapq import nlargest
from multiprocessing import Pool, cpu_count

from document_generator import Document

    SearchResult,
    tokenize,
    compute_term_frequencies,
)


@dataclass
class ParallelIndexingResult:
    """Result from parallel index building."""

    index: TFIDFIndex
    elapsed_time: float
    num_documents: int
    vocabulary_size: int


def _process_document_chunk(args: Tuple[List[Document], int]) -> Tuple[Dict, Dict, set]:
    """
    Process a chunk of documents to compute TF and collect vocabulary.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (documents_chunk, chunk_id)

    Returns:
        Tuple of (doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary)
    """
    documents, chunk_id = args
    doc_term_freqs = {}
    doc_terms = {}
    vocabulary = set()

    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.title + " " + doc.content
        tokens = tokenize(text)
        tf = compute_term_frequencies(tokens)
        doc_term_freqs[doc.doc_id] = tf
        doc_terms[doc.doc_id] = set(tf.keys())
        vocabulary.update(tf.keys())

    return doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary


def _compute_inverted_index_chunk(args: Tuple[List[str], Dict, Dict]) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[int, float]]]:
    """
    Compute inverted index for a subset of vocabulary terms.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf_scores)

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping terms to their posting lists
    """
    terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf = args
    inverted_index_chunk = {}

    for term in terms_subset:
        posting_list = []
        for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
            if term in tf_dict:
                tf = tf_dict[term]
                tfidf = tf * idf[term]
                posting_list.append((doc_id, tfidf))

        # Sort by score descending for efficient top-k retrieval
        posting_list.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        inverted_index_chunk[term] = posting_list

    return inverted_index_chunk


def build_tfidf_index_parallel(
    documents: List[Document],
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    chunk_size: int = 500,
) -> ParallelIndexingResult:
    """
    Build TF-IDF inverted index in parallel.

    Steps:
    1. Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
    2. Merge intermediate results
    3. Calculate document frequencies
    4. Compute IDF scores
    5. Build inverted index in parallel
    6. Compute document vector norms

    Args:
        documents: List of Document objects to index
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        chunk_size: Number of documents per chunk

    Returns:
        ParallelIndexingResult with the built index and timing info
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Use larger chunk sizes to amortize multiprocessing overhead
    effective_chunk_size = max(chunk_size, len(documents) // (num_workers * 2))

    index = TFIDFIndex()
    index.num_documents = len(documents)

    # Create a single Pool for all parallel operations
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Step 1: Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
        chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(documents), effective_chunk_size):
            chunk = documents[i : i + effective_chunk_size]
            chunks.append((chunk, i // effective_chunk_size))

        # Process chunks in parallel
        results = pool.map(_process_document_chunk, chunks)

        # Merge results from all chunks
        doc_term_freqs = {}
        doc_terms = {}
        vocabulary = set()

        for chunk_doc_term_freqs, chunk_doc_terms, chunk_vocab in results:
            doc_term_freqs.update(chunk_doc_term_freqs)
            doc_terms.update(chunk_doc_terms)
            vocabulary.update(chunk_vocab)

        index.vocabulary = vocabulary

        # Step 2: Calculate document frequencies (sequential but lightweight)
        for term in vocabulary:
            df = sum(1 for doc_id in doc_terms if term in doc_terms[doc_id])
            index.document_frequencies[term] = df

        # Step 3: Compute IDF scores (sequential but fast)
        N = index.num_documents
        for term, df in index.document_frequencies.items():
            index.idf[term] = math.log(N / df) + 1

        # Step 4: Build inverted index in parallel
        vocab_list = list(vocabulary)
        # Each worker processes a chunk of vocabulary
        vocab_chunk_size = max(1, len(vocab_list) // num_workers)
        vocab_chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(vocab_list), vocab_chunk_size):
            chunk = vocab_list[i : i + vocab_chunk_size]
            vocab_chunks.append((chunk, doc_term_freqs, index.idf))

        inverted_index_chunks = pool.map(_compute_inverted_index_chunk, vocab_chunks)

        # Merge inverted index chunks
        for chunk in inverted_index_chunks:
            index.inverted_index.update(chunk)

    # Step 5: Build document vectors and compute norms (parallel)
    # Create a list of (doc_id, tf_dict) tuples
    doc_id_tf_pairs = [(doc_id, tf_dict) for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items()]

    # Process in parallel using the existing pool
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Define a worker function
        def _compute_doc_vector(args_tuple):
            doc_id, tf_dict = args_tuple
            doc_vector = {}
            norm_squared = 0.0
            for term, tf in tf_dict.items():
                tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
                doc_vector[term] = tfidf
                norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf
            return doc_id, doc_vector, math.sqrt(norm_squared)

        # Process documents in parallel
        doc_vector_results = pool.map(_compute_doc_vector, doc_id_tf_pairs)

        # Merge results
        for doc_id, doc_vector, doc_norm in doc_vector_results:
            index.doc_vectors[doc_id] = doc_vector
            index.doc_norms[doc_id] = doc_norm

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return ParallelIndexingResult(
        index=index,
        elapsed_time=elapsed,
        num_documents=len(documents),
        vocabulary_size=len(vocabulary),
    )


def _search_single_query(query: str, index: TFIDFIndex, top_k: int, doc_titles: Dict[int, str]) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """
    Search for a single query.

    Args:
        query: Search query string
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results to return
        doc_titles: Dictionary mapping doc_id to title

    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects
    """
    # Tokenize query
    query_tokens = tokenize(query)
    if not query_tokens:
        return []

    # Compute query TF
    query_tf = compute_term_frequencies(query_tokens)

    # Compute query TF-IDF vector
    query_vector = {}
    query_norm_squared = 0.0
    for term, tf in query_tf.items():
        if term in index.idf:
            tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
            query_vector[term] = tfidf
            query_norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf

    if not query_vector:
        return []

    query_norm = math.sqrt(query_norm_squared)

    # Find candidate documents
    candidate_docs = set()
    for term in query_vector:
        if term in index.inverted_index:
            for doc_id, _ in index.inverted_index[term]:
                candidate_docs.add(doc_id)

    # Compute cosine similarity for each candidate
    scores = []
    for doc_id in candidate_docs:
        doc_vector = index.doc_vectors.get(doc_id, {})
        doc_norm = index.doc_norms.get(doc_id, 0)

        if doc_norm == 0:
            continue

        # Dot product
        dot_product = sum(query_vector.get(term, 0) * doc_vector.get(term, 0) for term in query_vector)

        # Cosine similarity
        similarity = dot_product / (query_norm * doc_norm)
        scores.append((doc_id, similarity))

    # Get top-k results
    top_results = nlargest(top_k, scores, key=lambda x: x[1])

    # Build result objects
    results = []
    for doc_id, score in top_results:
        results.append(SearchResult(doc_id=doc_id, score=score, title=doc_titles.get(doc_id, f"Document {doc_id}")))

    return results


def batch_search_parallel(
    queries: List[str],
    index: TFIDFIndex,
    top_k: int = 10,
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    documents: Optional[List[Document]] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[List[SearchResult]], float]:
    """
    Search for multiple queries in parallel using ThreadPoolExecutor.

    Args:
        queries: List of search query strings
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results per query
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        documents: Optional list of documents for title lookup

    Returns:
        Tuple of (list of result lists, elapsed_time)
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Build doc_titles once to avoid passing documents list
    doc_titles = {d.doc_id: d.title for d in documents} if documents else {}

    # Use ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel search
    # This avoids pickling overhead while allowing concurrent execution
    results = [None] * len(queries)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_workers) as executor:
        # Submit all queries
        future_to_query = {
            executor.submit(_search_single_query, query, index, top_k, doc_titles): i
            for i, query in enumerate(queries)
        }

        # Collect results as they complete
        for future in as_completed(future_to_query):
            idx = future_to_query[future]
            results[idx] = future.result()

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return results, elapsed


def main():

    parser.add_argument("--corpus", type=str, default=None, help="Path to corpus JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--num-docs", type=int, default=5000, help="Number of documents to generate if no corpus provided")
    parser.add_argument("--query", type=str, default="machine learning algorithm", help="Search query")
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=10, help="Number of top results to return")
    parser.add_argument("--num-workers", type=int, default=None, help="Number of parallel workers")
    parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=500, help="Chunk size for document processing")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    print("=" * 60)
    print("Parallel TF-IDF Search Engine")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Import here to avoid circular imports
    from document_generator import load_corpus, generate_corpus

    # Load or generate corpus
    if args.corpus:
        print(f"\nLoading corpus from {args.corpus}...")
        documents = load_corpus(args.corpus)
    else:
        print(f"\nGenerating {args.num_docs} documents...")
        documents = generate_corpus(args.num_docs, seed=42)

    print(f"Corpus size: {len(documents)} documents")
    total_words = sum(d.word_count for d in documents)
    print(f"Total words: {total_words:,}")
    print(f"Using {args.num_workers or cpu_count()} workers")

    # Build index
    print("\nBuilding TF-IDF index in parallel...")
    result = build_tfidf_index_parallel(documents, num_workers=args.num_workers, chunk_size=args.chunk_size)

    print(f"\nIndex built in {result.elapsed_time:.3f} seconds")
    print(f"Vocabulary size: {result.vocabulary_size:,} terms")
    print(f"Documents indexed: {result.num_documents}")

    # Perform search
    print(f"\nSearching for: '{args.query}'")
    print("-" * 60)

    search_results, search_time = batch_search_parallel(
        [args.query],
        result.index,
        args.top_k,
        num_workers=args.num_workers,
        documents=documents,
    )

    print(f"Search completed in {search_time*1000:.2f} ms")
    print(f"\nTop {len(search_results[0])} results:")
    for i, res in enumerate(search_results[0], 1):
        print(f"  {i}. [{res.score:.4f}] {res.title} (doc_id: {res.doc_id})")

    return result, search_results

    main()

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping terms to their posting lists
    """
    terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf = args
    inverted_index_chunk = {}

    for term in terms_subset:
        posting_list = []
        for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
            if term in tf_dict:
                tf = tf_dict[term]
                tfidf = tf * idf[term]
                posting_list.append((doc_id, tfidf))

        # Sort by score descending for efficient top-k retrieval
        posting_list.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        inverted_index_chunk[term] = posting_list

    return inverted_index_chunk


def build_tfidf_index_parallel(
    documents: List[Document],
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    chunk_size: int = 500,
) -> ParallelIndexingResult:
    """
    Build TF-IDF inverted index in parallel.

    Steps:
    1. Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
    2. Merge intermediate results
    3. Calculate document frequencies
    4. Compute IDF scores
    5. Build inverted index in parallel
    6. Compute document vector norms

    Args:
        documents: List of Document objects to index
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        chunk_size: Number of documents per chunk

    Returns:
        ParallelIndexingResult with the built index and timing info
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Use larger chunk sizes to amortize multiprocessing overhead
    effective_chunk_size = max(chunk_size, len(documents) // (num_workers * 2))

    index = TFIDFIndex()
    index.num_documents = len(documents)

    # Create a single Pool for all parallel operations
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Step 1: Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
        chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(documents), effective_chunk_size):
            chunk = documents[i : i + effective_chunk_size]
            chunks.append((chunk, i // effective_chunk_size))

        # Process chunks in parallel
        results = pool.map(_process_document_chunk, chunks)

        # Merge results from all chunks
        doc_term_freqs = {}
        doc_terms = {}
        vocabulary = set()

        for chunk_doc_term_freqs, chunk_doc_terms, chunk_vocab in results:
            doc_term_freqs.update(chunk_doc_term_freqs)
            doc_terms.update(chunk_doc_terms)
            vocabulary.update(chunk_vocab)

        index.vocabulary = vocabulary

        # Step 2: Calculate document frequencies (sequential but lightweight)
        for term in vocabulary:
            df = sum(1 for doc_id in doc_terms if term in doc_terms[doc_id])
            index.document_frequencies[term] = df

        # Step 3: Compute IDF scores (sequential but fast)
        N = index.num_documents
        for term, df in index.document_frequencies.items():
            index.idf[term] = math.log(N / df) + 1

        # Step 4: Build inverted index in parallel
        vocab_list = list(vocabulary)
        # Each worker processes a chunk of vocabulary
        vocab_chunk_size = max(1, len(vocab_list) // num_workers)
        vocab_chunks = []
        for i in range(0, len(vocab_list), vocab_chunk_size):
            chunk = vocab_list[i : i + vocab_chunk_size]
            vocab_chunks.append((chunk, doc_term_freqs, index.idf))

        inverted_index_chunks = pool.map(_compute_inverted_index_chunk, vocab_chunks)

        # Merge inverted index chunks
        for chunk in inverted_index_chunks:
            index.inverted_index.update(chunk)

    # Step 5: Build document vectors and compute norms (parallel)
    # Create a list of (doc_id, tf_dict) tuples
    doc_id_tf_pairs = [(doc_id, tf_dict) for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items()]

    # Process in parallel using the existing pool
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:
        # Define a worker function
        def _compute_doc_vector(args_tuple):
            doc_id, tf_dict = args_tuple
            doc_vector = {}
            norm_squared = 0.0
            for term, tf in tf_dict.items():
                tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
                doc_vector[term] = tfidf
                norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf
            return doc_id, doc_vector, math.sqrt(norm_squared)

        # Process documents in parallel
        doc_vector_results = pool.map(_compute_doc_vector, doc_id_tf_pairs)

        # Merge results
        for doc_id, doc_vector, doc_norm in doc_vector_results:
            index.doc_vectors[doc_id] = doc_vector
            index.doc_norms[doc_id] = doc_norm

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return ParallelIndexingResult(
        index=index,
        elapsed_time=elapsed,
        num_documents=len(documents),
        vocabulary_size=len(vocabulary),
    )


def _search_single_query(query: str, index: TFIDFIndex, top_k: int, doc_titles: Dict[int, str]) -> List[SearchResult]:
    """
    Search for a single query.

    Args:
        query: Search query string
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results to return
        doc_titles: Dictionary mapping doc_id to title

    Returns:
        List of SearchResult objects
    """
    # Tokenize query
    query_tokens = tokenize(query)
    if not query_tokens:
        return []

    # Compute query TF
    query_tf = compute_term_frequencies(query_tokens)

    # Compute query TF-IDF vector
    query_vector = {}
    query_norm_squared = 0.0
    for term, tf in query_tf.items():
        if term in index.idf:
            tfidf = tf * index.idf[term]
            query_vector[term] = tfidf
            query_norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf

    if not query_vector:
        return []

    query_norm = math.sqrt(query_norm_squared)

    # Find candidate documents
    candidate_docs = set()
    for term in query_vector:
        if term in index.inverted_index:
            for doc_id, _ in index.inverted_index[term]:
                candidate_docs.add(doc_id)

    # Compute cosine similarity for each candidate
    scores = []
    for doc_id in candidate_docs:
        doc_vector = index.doc_vectors.get(doc_id, {})
        doc_norm = index.doc_norms.get(doc_id, 0)

        if doc_norm == 0:
            continue

        # Dot product
        dot_product = sum(query_vector.get(term, 0) * doc_vector.get(term, 0) for term in query_vector)

        # Cosine similarity
        similarity = dot_product / (query_norm * doc_norm)
        scores.append((doc_id, similarity))

    # Get top-k results
    top_results = nlargest(top_k, scores, key=lambda x: x[1])

    # Build result objects
    results = []
    for doc_id, score in top_results:
        results.append(SearchResult(doc_id=doc_id, score=score, title=doc_titles.get(doc_id, f"Document {doc_id}")))

    return results


def batch_search_parallel(
    queries: List[str],
    index: TFIDFIndex,
    top_k: int = 10,
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    documents: Optional[List[Document]] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[List[SearchResult]], float]:
    """
    Search for multiple queries in parallel using ThreadPoolExecutor.

    Args:
        queries: List of search query strings
        index: TF-IDF index to search
        top_k: Number of top results per query
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        documents: Optional list of documents for title lookup

    Returns:
        Tuple of (list of result lists, elapsed_time)
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Build doc_titles once to avoid passing documents list
    doc_titles = {d.doc_id: d.title for d in documents} if documents else {}

    # Use ThreadPoolExecutor for parallel search
    # This avoids pickling overhead while allowing concurrent execution
    results = [None] * len(queries)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=num_workers) as executor:
        # Submit all queries
        future_to_query = {
            executor.submit(_search_single_query, query, index, top_k, doc_titles): i
            for i, query in enumerate(queries)
        }

        # Collect results as they complete
        for future in as_completed(future_to_query):
            idx = future_to_query[future]
            results[idx] = future.result()

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_time

    return results, elapsed


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Parallel TF-IDF indexing and search")
    parser.add_argument("--corpus", type=str, default=None, help="Path to corpus JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--num-docs", type=int, default=5000, help="Number of documents to generate if no corpus provided")
    parser.add_argument("--query", type=str, default="machine learning algorithm", help="Search query")
    parser.add_argument("--top-k", type=int, default=10, help="Number of top results to return")
    parser.add_argument("--num-workers", type=int, default=None, help="Number of parallel workers")
    parser.add_argument("--chunk-size", type=int, default=500, help="Chunk size for document processing")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    print("=" * 60)
    print("Parallel TF-IDF Search Engine")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Import here to avoid circular imports
    from document_generator import load_corpus, generate_corpus

    # Load or generate corpus
    if args.corpus:
        print(f"\nLoading corpus from {args.corpus}...")
        documents = load_corpus(args.corpus)
    else:
        print(f"\nGenerating {args.num_docs} documents...")
        documents = generate_corpus(args.num_docs, seed=42)

    print(f"Corpus size: {len(documents)} documents")
    total_words = sum(d.word_count for d in documents)
    print(f"Total words: {total_words:,}")
    print(f"Using {args.num_workers or cpu_count()} workers")

    # Build index
    print("\nBuilding TF-IDF index in parallel...")
    result = build_tfidf_index_parallel(documents, num_workers=args.num_workers, chunk_size=args.chunk_size)

    print(f"\nIndex built in {result.elapsed_time:.3f} seconds")
    print(f"Vocabulary size: {result.vocabulary_size:,} terms")
    print(f"Documents indexed: {result.num_documents}")

    # Perform search
    print(f"\nSearching for: '{args.query}'")
    print("-" * 60)

    search_results, search_time = batch_search_parallel(
        [args.query],
        result.index,
        args.top_k,
        num_workers=args.num_workers,
        documents=documents,
    )

    print(f"Search completed in {search_time*1000:.2f} ms")
    print(f"\nTop {len(search_results[0])} results:")
    for i, res in enumerate(search_results[0], 1):
        print(f"  {i}. [{res.score:.4f}] {res.title} (doc_id: {res.doc_id})")

    return result, search_results


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Parallel TF-IDF Implementation - Optimized Version

This module provides a parallel implementation of:
1. TF-IDF index building using multiprocessing
2. Parallel cosine similarity search using threading

Achieves performance improvements through:
- Document chunking for parallel index building
- Query parallelization for batch search

import argparse
import math
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from heapq import nlargest
from multiprocessing import Pool, cpu_count
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional

from document_generator import Document
from sequential import (
    TFIDFIndex,
    SearchResult,
    tokenize,
    compute_term_frequencies,
)


@dataclass
class ParallelIndexingResult:
    """Result from parallel index building."""

    index: TFIDFIndex
    elapsed_time: float
    num_documents: int
    vocabulary_size: int


def _process_document_chunk(args: Tuple[List[Document], int]) -> Tuple[Dict, Dict, set]:
    """
    Process a chunk of documents to compute TF and collect vocabulary.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (documents_chunk, chunk_id)

    Returns:
        Tuple of (doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary)
    """
    documents, chunk_id = args
    doc_term_freqs = {}
    doc_terms = {}
    vocabulary = set()

    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.title + " " + doc.content
        tokens = tokenize(text)
        tf = compute_term_frequencies(tokens)
        doc_term_freqs[doc.doc_id] = tf
        doc_terms[doc.doc_id] = set(tf.keys())
        vocabulary.update(tf.keys())

    return doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary


def _compute_inverted_index_chunk(args: Tuple[List[str], Dict, Dict]) -> Dict[str, List[Tuple[int, float]]]:
    """
    Compute inverted index for a subset of vocabulary terms.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf_scores)

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping terms to their posting lists
    """
    terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf = args
    inverted_index_chunk = {}

    for term in terms_subset:
        posting_list = []
        for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
            if term in tf_dict:
                tf = tf_dict[term]
                tfidf = tf * idf[term]
                posting_list.append((doc_id, tfidf))

        # Sort by score descending for efficient top-k retrieval
        posting_list.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        inverted_index_chunk[term] = posting_list

    return inverted_index_chunk


def _compute_doc_vector_pair(args_tuple: Tuple[int, Dict[str, float], Dict[str, float]]) -> Tuple[int, Dict[str, float], float]:
    """
    Compute document vector and norm for a single document.

    Args:
        args_tuple: Tuple of (doc_id, tf_dict, idf)

    Returns:
        Tuple of (doc_id, doc_vector, doc_norm)
    """
    doc_id, tf_dict, idf = args_tuple
    doc_vector = {}
    norm_squared = 0.0
    for term, tf in tf_dict.items():
        tfidf = tf * idf[term]
        doc_vector[term] = tfidf
        norm_squared += tfidf * tfidf
    return doc_id, doc_vector, math.sqrt(norm_squared)


def build_tfidf_index_parallel(
    documents: List[Document],
    num_workers: Optional[int] = None,
    chunk_size: int = 500,
) -> ParallelIndexingResult:
    """
    Build TF-IDF inverted index in parallel.

    Steps:
    1. Split documents into chunks and process in parallel
    2. Merge intermediate results
    3. Calculate document frequencies
    4. Compute IDF scores
    5. Build inverted index in parallel
    6. Compute document vector norms

    Args:
        documents: List of Document objects to index
        num_workers: Number of parallel workers (default: CPU count)
        chunk_size: Number of documents per chunk

    Returns:
        ParallelIndexingResult with the built index and timing info
    """
    start_time = time.perf_counter()

    # Determine number of workers
    if num_workers is None:
        num_workers = cpu_count()

    # Use larger chunk sizes to amortize multiprocessing overhead
    effective_chunk_size = max(chunk_size, len(documents) // (num_workers * 2))

    index = TFIDFIndex()
    index.num_documents = len(documents)

    # Create a single Pool for all parallel operations
    with Pool(num_workers) as pool:

    """
    Process a chunk of documents to compute TF and collect vocabulary.

    Args:
        args: Tuple of (documents_chunk, chunk_id)

    Returns:
        Tuple of (doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary)
    """
    documents, chunk_id = args
    doc_term_freqs = {}
    doc_terms = {}
    vocabulary = set()

    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.title + " " + doc.content
        tokens = tokenize(text)
        tf = compute_term_frequencies(tokens)
        doc_term_freqs[doc.doc_id] = tf
        doc_terms[doc.doc_id] = set(tf.keys())
        vocabulary.update(tf.keys())

    return doc_term_freqs, doc_terms, vocabulary

    Compute inverted index for a subset of vocabulary terms.

    Args:

    Returns:
        Dictionary mapping terms to their posting lists
    """
    terms_subset, doc_term_freqs, idf = args
    inverted_index_chunk = {}

    for term in terms_subset:
        posting_list = []
        for doc_id, tf_dict in doc_term_freqs.items():
            if term in tf_dict:
                tf = tf_dict[term]
                tfidf = tf * idf[term]
                posting_list.append((doc_id, tfidf))

        # Sort by score descending for efficient top-k retrieval
        posting_list.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        inverted_index_chunk[term] = posting_list

    return inverted_index_chunk

    return doc_id, doc_vector, math.sqrt(norm_squared)
